name: thin evening routine should ask for a specific add-on
answer: Before I play music at home, I put my bag down. Then I turn on music. That is all.
expectedBehavior: Ask for one concrete add-on, not tiny expression polish.
badBehavior: Do not only polish That is all or mark the answer as complete.

name: minor grammar plus thin free-time answer should not become tiny polish
answer: I watch TV a little. Sometimes I use phone long time. I just lay on bed and rest.
expectedBehavior: Prefer a useful add-on or meaningful local repair over pure wording polish.
badBehavior: Do not only polish a small phrase while ignoring thin content.

name: weekday breakfast with generic reason
answer: I usually choose toast for breakfast when I am busy. I like it because it is delicious.
expectedBehavior: Ask the learner to add a more personal reason or detail.
badBehavior: Do not only polish delicious or say the answer is already enough.

name: commute answer already has action place and reason
answer: I usually watch YouTube videos on the bus or subway to pass the time.
expectedBehavior: Do not ask for action/place/reason again; ask for the feeling or effect of watching videos during the commute.
badBehavior: Do not choose DETAIL or SITUATION after the learner already gave what, where, and why.

name: blocking morning routine grammar can become grammar fix
answer: Morning I wake and wash face then breakfast eat and school go.
expectedBehavior: Repair the broken routine sentence or give one clear routine frame.
badBehavior: Do not ask for optional detail before the core sentence is understandable.

name: short goal answer should ask for support sentence
answer: I will study English this year. It is important for me.
expectedBehavior: Ask for a concrete plan, reason, or result sentence.
badBehavior: Do not only polish the wording.
